QF.id: XIII Introduction to the Underlying Markets_44

question.text: In the Indian government securities market, what is the difference between a 'yield-based auction' and a 'price-based auction'?

answer.text: Yield-based auctions are used for new securities where bidders bid in terms of yield; price-based auctions are used for reissued securities where bidders bid in terms of price
Yield-based auctions are for short-term T-Bills; price-based auctions are for long-term bonds
Yield-based auctions are conducted by SEBI; price-based auctions are conducted by RBI
There is no difference — both terms refer to the same auction mechanism

explanation.text: The Logic: In India's primary G-Sec auctions conducted by RBI, the auction method depends on whether the security is new or a reissue. For a new security with no existing coupon, bidders submit bids in terms of yield, and the cut-off yield determines the coupon. For a reissue of an already-trading security, the coupon is fixed, so bidders submit bids in terms of price (which determines the yield to the buyer). The Trap: Both yield-based and price-based auctions are conducted by RBI (not split between SEBI and RBI), and both are used across T-Bills and longer-dated G-Secs — the distinction is new versus reissued, not short versus long tenor. They are also genuinely different mechanisms, so they are not the same thing. Note: The specific new-issue-versus-reissue distinction for yield-based vs price-based auctions was not located in the cited Series IV workbook page (p.71). The framing above is general Indian G-Sec primary market knowledge, not a workbook citation.
